name: Lunasin
lead: Lunasin is a 43-amino-acid peptide found in soybean and some cereal grains, sold as a soy-derived dietary supplement [1][2]. People take it for general wellness goals such as cholesterol, inflammation and cellular health, and in appearance communities it is mentioned as part of longevity and skin-and-body upkeep stacks, where lower inflammation and better cardiometabolic health are seen as supporting a healthier look.

A soybean cDNA encoding a chromatin-binding peptide was described in 1999, and later laboratory work reported that the peptide binds histones and inhibits their acetylation [3][4]. Most research has been in cell and animal models of cancer prevention and inflammation [5][6].
Human data are small. A crossover trial of lunasin-enriched soy extract measured cardiometabolic markers [7], and a year-long open-label ALS trial found that it did not slow progression [8].

angle.text: People use lunasin as a wellness supplement for inflammation and cardiometabolic health, hoping that better overall health shows in skin and physique. Its anti-inflammatory activity has been studied mainly in cells.

card.summary: A soy-derived peptide supplement taken for inflammation and cardiometabolic support, which some users hope translates into healthier-looking skin and body.
card.note: Human trials are few and small.

quick.overview:
Lunasin is a short peptide found in soybeans and some grains, and it is sold as a capsule or powder supplement. The name comes from the Filipino word for cure.

People take it for cholesterol, inflammation and general health. Appearance-focused users include it in recovery and longevity stacks.
quick.mechanism: In laboratory studies lunasin binds histones, reduces inflammatory signalling in macrophages and shows antioxidant activity [3][4]. It has been detected in plasma after soy protein intake [13].
quick.risks: A year-long ALS trial reported more gastrointestinal side effects than expected [8]. It is a supplement, so products vary and are not approved to treat disease. People with soy allergy would encounter soy-derived material.

paras: Lunasin is a 43-residue peptide with a run of aspartic acid residues, an RGD cell-adhesion motif and a region resembling chromatin-binding proteins [3]. It occurs in soy and in cereals and amaranth seeds [9][10].

Laboratory work reports that lunasin binds deacetylated histones and inhibits acetylation [3]. Studies in macrophage cells report suppression of the NF-kappaB inflammatory pathway and antioxidant activity [6][11]. Soy protease inhibitors were reported to help it survive digestion [12], and lunasin has been found in human plasma after soy protein consumption [13].

A triple-blind crossover trial in 31 older adults compared an 8-week course of lunasin-enriched soy extract to placebo for lipids, glucose, insulin and blood pressure [7]. A single-center, year-long trial with historical controls in 60 people with ALS reported that lunasin did not slow progression [8][14]. A small trial of soy-based supplements on cardiometabolic risk factors in obesity was also registered [15]. No studies have tested lunasin for skin or appearance outcomes.
Lunasin appears in discussions of supplement stacks aimed at inflammation, cholesterol and longevity. Proponents frame lower inflammation and better metabolic health as the route to a healthier look.

timeline.event: A soybean cDNA encoding a chromatin-binding peptide that inhibits mitosis in mammalian cells is reported [4].
Lunasin is reported to bind deacetylated histones and inhibit acetylation [3].
A year-long ALS trial of a lunasin regimen reports no slowing of progression [8].
